strengths: A meaningful contribution to interpretability security: shaping optimization trajectories through weight updates enables deceptive feature visualizations without conspicuous architectural modifications. The tunnel construction offers a distinct mechanism relative to prior attacks.

The central vulnerability has substantial empirical support across CNNs, vision transformers, multiple datasets, and visualization procedures, including transfer to MACO. For ResNet-50, target-image CLIP similarity improves from 0.53 to 0.69 while accuracy decreases from 76.13% to 75.13% and target-feature AUROC remains approximately unchanged.

The supplementary experiments strengthen the evidence through ten additional output-neuron attacks, alternative target images, model-capacity experiments, and explicit accuracy–manipulation trade-offs. These results establish a useful capability and support acceptance.

The presentation is clear, with an intuitive toy example and extensive implementation, hyperparameter, data-source, and compute details. A code link supports reproducibility. Limitations and dual-use implications are acknowledged appropriately; the manuscript presents no evident serious ethical concern.
weaknesses: Preservation of internal representations is stronger than the measurements establish. Classification accuracy and feature AUROC do not demonstrate unchanged activations or causal mechanisms, and inspecting other output visualizations provides only indirect evidence. In the CLIP case, w=1 removes the full-representation preservation term entirely. Direct held-out representation comparisons would better support this central distinction from prior work.

The claim of arbitrary target visualization needs qualification. Results depend on model capacity and target content; some smaller models suffer substantial accuracy losses. For ViT-L/32 at the selected alpha=0.9995, Table 21 shows improved text alignment but no improvement in target-image CLIP similarity or LPIPS. Broader feature–target sampling would establish reliability beyond the demonstrated examples.

The ProxPulse comparison covers one model–feature–target configuration and only two reported trade-off settings. Matched tuning budgets and an ablation isolating the tunnel construction from the preservation objective would strengthen the claimed methodological advantage.

Lemma 3.1 establishes convergence for an exactly prescribed quadratic gradient field, rather than its realization through fine-tuning. Equation (5) also lacks boundary compatibility conditions. Additionally, the stated slingshot radius of 0.01 does not encompass typical high-dimensional initializations with per-coordinate standard deviation 0.01 under the stated Euclidean-ball definition; the sampling convention needs clarification.

Natural-example inspection is a useful cross-check, but the evidence does not establish a reliable attack detector: no operational decision rule, false-positive evaluation on clean models, or adaptive-attack evaluation is provided. The proposed sparse-autoencoder/attribution audit is hypothetical, so the claim that discovery becomes effectively impossible exceeds the demonstrated case study.

Reported uncertainty mainly measures visualization randomness for fixed manipulated models, not variability across independent attack training runs. Reporting inconsistencies also need correction: Table 3 states 100 CLIP visualization runs whereas Appendix C.8 specifies 30, and Table 16 reverses the accuracy and AUROC column headings.
